sections.title: Scenario
sections.prompt: Who uses the platform, what must it detect, and which numbers shape the design?
criteria: Converts 42M spans a day into average and peak spans per second and bytes per day
Defines one business success metric per agent, not only a judge score
Shows that judging every run is unaffordable inside the $50k budget, with arithmetic
States the 30 minute detection target as the headline requirement

sections.title: Single View
sections.prompt: Draw the path from an agent run to a page and to a CI block.
criteria: Uses OpenTelemetry or an equivalent standard with async export from the agent
Puts an event log between collection and the stores and evaluators
Separates online evals, offline gates and human review as distinct layers
Tags every span with prompt, model and tool versions

sections.title: Data Sources
sections.prompt: Which signals feed quality, and which ones mislead?
criteria: Uses business outcomes from systems of record (reopens, disputes), not only thumbs
Records change events (deploys of prompts, models, tools, indexes) as data
Notes that explicit feedback is sparse and biased

sections.title: Processing
sections.prompt: What is sampled, what is computed in stream, and how is one tenant kept from flooding the pipeline?
criteria: Uses tail sampling that keeps all errors and negative-feedback runs
Keeps metadata for 100 percent of runs even when content is sampled
Computes windowed metrics per agent at a window short enough for the 30 minute target
Enforces a per-tenant ingest quota

sections.title: Agents
sections.prompt: Which judges and models score runs, what do they cost, and how do you trust them?
criteria: Prices the judge per run and per month from token counts
Calibrates the judge against human labels with a named agreement statistic and threshold
Runs pairwise judgments in both orders to cancel position bias
Sizes any self-hosted scoring model in GPUs from a throughput number

sections.title: Memory
sections.prompt: What does the platform keep over time to compare against?
criteria: Keeps a reference window for drift baselines
Versions golden sets with slices and must-pass cases
Links golden cases to their source run so erasure cascades

sections.title: MCP Tool Servers
sections.prompt: What tools does the platform expose to agents, and with what limits?
criteria: Exposes trace search and run lookup as read-only tools
Scopes tool results by the caller's team and tenant grants
Denies agents any write access to golden sets or scores

sections.title: Endpoints
sections.prompt: What endpoints exist, and how long from a bad run to a page?
criteria: Keeps span export off the agent's critical path, dropping rather than blocking
Gives a stage-by-stage latency budget from run to page under 30 minutes
Gives offline eval traffic its own provider quota
Makes gate runs durable so a CI retry does not pay twice

sections.title: Caching
sections.prompt: What is cached to save judge cost and gate time, and what invalidates it?
criteria: Keys cached judge scores on rubric version and judge model, not only input
Reuses unchanged offline outputs between pull request reruns
Prompt-caches the judge rubric prefix

sections.title: Data Stores
sections.prompt: Where do metadata and content live, how big are they, and what does it all cost?
criteria: Sizes hot and cold storage from spans per day, bytes per span and retention
Stores content separately from metrics
Gives a monthly cost breakdown that fits the $50k budget
Explains how GDPR erasure works in append-only storage

sections.title: Output
sections.prompt: What does a team or on-call engineer actually receive?
criteria: Gate results show failed must-pass cases and slice deltas with uncertainty
Pages include the most recent change event before the drop
Reports cost per successful run alongside quality

sections.title: Guardrails
sections.prompt: What makes the gate honest, and what limits cost and data exposure?
criteria: Sets a gate threshold justified by the standard error at the golden-set size
Uses a paired test or design across old and new versions
Requires a named approver to override a block
Caps eval spend per team in code

sections.title: Key Impact
sections.prompt: Which numbers prove the platform works, and how are they measured?
criteria: Gives baseline and target for detection time
Measures the share of changes that passed a gate
Measures judge agreement on a recurring human-labeled audit

sections.title: Failure Modes
sections.prompt: What breaks in the eval system itself?
criteria: Covers the judge model changing underneath you
Covers agents with too little traffic for the sample rate
States what fails open for the agent and what fails closed for the gate

sections.title: Build Order
sections.prompt: In what order do you build it, and what number ends each phase?
criteria: Ships tracing and cheap signals before LLM judges
Ends each phase with a measured number
Fits the plan in 26 weeks for 6 engineers
